title: 考研英语（旧）2007年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: If you were to examine the birth certificates of every soccer player in 2006's World Cup tournament, you would most likely find a noteworthy quirk: elite soccer players are more likely to have been born in the earlier months of the year than in the later months.
sentences.translation: 如果你查看2006年世界杯锦标赛中每位足球运动员的出生证明，你很可能会发现一个值得注意的怪现象：精英足球运动员更有可能出生在一年中较早的月份，而不是较晚的月份。如果你接着查看为世界杯和职业队伍输送人才的欧洲国家青年队，你会发现这一奇怪现象更加明显。

sentences.text: If you then examined the European national youth teams that feed the World Cup and professional ranks, you would find this strange phenomenon to be even more pronounced.

sentences.text: Ericsson grew up in Sweden, and studied nuclear engineering until he realized he would have more opportunity to conduct his own research if he switched to psychology.
His first experiment, nearly 30 years ago, involved memory: training a person to hear and then repeat a random series of numbers.

This success, coupled with later research showing that memory itself is not genetically determined, led Ericsson to conclude that the act of memorizing is more of a cognitive exercise than an intuitive one.
sentences.translation: 这一成功，加上后来的研究表明记忆本身并非由基因决定，使Ericsson得出结论：记忆行为更多是一种认知练习而非直觉练习。换句话说，两个人在记忆能力上可能表现出的任何先天差异，都会被每个人如何"编码"信息所掩盖。而学习如何有意义地编码信息的最佳方法，Ericsson确定，是一个被称为刻意练习的过程。刻意练习不仅仅是简单地重复一项任务，而是涉及设定具体目标、获得即时反馈，以及同时关注技巧和结果。

sentences.text: In other words, whatever inborn differences two people may exhibit in their abilities to memorize, those differences are swamped by how well each person "encodes" the information.
And the best way to learn how to encode information meaningfully, Ericsson determined, was a process known as deliberate practice.
Deliberate practice entails more than simply repeating a task.
Rather, it involves setting specific goals, obtaining immediate feedback and concentrating as much on technique as on outcome.
Ericsson and his colleagues have thus taken to studying expert performers in a wide range of pursuits, including soccer.
sentences.translation: 因此，Ericsson和他的同事们开始研究广泛领域的专家表现者，包括足球。他们收集所有能收集到的数据，不仅是表现统计数据和传记细节，还包括他们自己与高成就者进行的实验室实验结果。他们的工作提出了一个相当惊人的断言：我们通常称为天赋的特质被高度高估了。或者换句话说，专家表现者——无论是在记忆还是外科手术、芭蕾还是计算机编程方面——几乎总是后天培养的，而非天生的。

sentences.text: They gather all the data they can, not just performance statistics and biographical details but also the results of their own laboratory experiments with high achievers.
Their work makes a rather startling assertion: the trait we commonly call talent is highly overrated.
Or, put another way, expert performers – whether in memory or surgery, ballet or computer programming – are nearly always made, not born.

During the past generation, the American middle-class family that once could count on hard work and fair play to keep itself financially secure has been transformed by economic risk and new realities.
sentences.translation: 在过去一代人的时间里,曾经可以依靠努力工作和公平竞争来维持经济安全的美国中产阶级家庭,已经被经济风险和新现实所改变。现在,一张解雇通知书、一次糟糕的诊断或一位消失的配偶,就能在几个月内使一个家庭从稳固的中产阶级沦为新贫困者。

sentences.text: Now a pink slip, a bad diagnosis, or a disappearing spouse can reduce a family from solidly middle class to newly poor in a few months.
During the same period, families have been asked to absorb much more risk in their retirement income.
sentences.translation: 在同一时期,家庭被要求在退休收入方面承担更多风险。钢铁工人、航空公司员工,以及现在汽车行业的员工,正在加入数百万必须担心利率、股市波动以及可能会比退休金活得更久这一严酷现实的家庭行列。在过去一年的大部分时间里,Bush总统竞选时主张将社会保障转变为储蓄账户模式,让退休人员用他们大部分或全部有保障的支付换取取决于投资回报的支付。对于年轻家庭来说,情况并没有更好。医疗保健的绝对成本和家庭承担的份额都在上升——而新近流行的健康储蓄计划正从立法机构蔓延到Wal-Mart员工,伴随着更高的免赔额和家庭未来医疗保健的大量新增投资风险。甚至人口结构也在对中产阶级家庭不利,因为拥有身体虚弱的年迈父母——以及随之而来的所有身体和经济援助需求——的可能性在仅仅一代人的时间里就增加了八倍。

sentences.text: Steelworkers, airline employees, and now those in the auto industry are joining millions of families who must worry about interest rates, stock market fluctuation, and the harsh reality that they may outlive their retirement money.

For much of the past year, President Bush campaigned to move Social Security to a savings-account model, with retirees trading much or all of their guaranteed payments for payments depending on investment returns.
For younger families, the picture is not any better.

Both the absolute cost of healthcare and the share of it borne by families have risen – and newly fashionable health-savings plans are spreading from legislative halls to Wal-Mart workers, with much higher deductibles and a large new dose of investment risk for families' future healthcare.

Even demographics are working against the middle class family, as the odds of having a weak elderly parent – and all the attendant need for physical and financial assistance – have jumped eightfold in just one generation.

From the middle-class family perspective, much of this, understandably, looks far less like an opportunity to exercise more financial responsibility, and a good deal more like a frightening acceleration of the wholesale shift of financial risk onto their already overburdened shoulders.
sentences.translation: 从中产阶级家庭的角度来看,可以理解的是,这其中的大部分看起来远不像是一个行使更多财务责任的机会,而更像是财务风险向他们已经负担过重的肩膀大规模转移的可怕加速。财务影响已经开始显现,政治影响可能也不远了。

sentences.text: The financial fallout has begun, and the political fallout may not be far behind.
It never rains but it pours.
sentences.translation: 祸不单行。正当老板们和董事会终于解决了最糟糕的会计和合规问题,并改善了薄弱的公司治理时,一个新问题开始威胁着他们——尤其是在美国——可能招致那种不可避免地导致高管层人头落地的负面头条:数据不安全。信息保护直到现在还被留给级别较低的IT员工来处理,并且被视为只有银行、电信和航空旅行等数据密集型行业才关心的问题,如今却成为各类企业老板议程上的首要事项。

sentences.text: Just as bosses and boards have finally sorted out their worst accounting and compliance troubles, and improved their feeble corporation governance, a new problem threatens to earn them – especially in America – the sort of nasty headlines that inevitably lead to heads rolling in the executive suite: data insecurity.

Left, until now, to odd, low-level IT staff to put right, and seen as a concern only of data-rich industries such as banking, telecoms and air travel, information protection is now high on the boss's agenda in businesses of every variety.

Several massive leakages of customer and employee data this year – from organizations as diverse as Time Warner, the American defense contractor Science Applications International Corp and even the University of California, Berkeley – have left managers hurriedly peering into their intricate IT systems and business processes in search of potential vulnerabilities.
sentences.translation: 今年发生的几起大规模客户和员工数据泄露事件——涉及Time Warner、美国国防承包商ScienceApplications International Corp甚至加州大学伯克利分校等各类组织——已经让管理者们匆忙审视他们复杂的IT系统和业务流程,寻找潜在的漏洞。

sentences.text: "Data is becoming an asset which needs to be guarded as much as any other asset," says Haim Mendelson of Stanford University's business school.

"Setting theproper investment level for security, redundancy, and recovery is a management issue, not a technicalone," he says.斯坦福大学商学院的Haim Mendelson说:"数据正在成为一种需要像其他任何资产一样加以保护的资产。保护客户数据的能力是市场价值的关键,而董事会代表股东对此负有责任。"确实,正如存在公认会计原则(GAAP)的概念一样,纽约哥伦比亚商学院的Eli Noam建议,也许是时候制定GASP,即公认安全实践了。他说:"为安全、冗余和恢复设定适当的投资水平是一个管理问题,而不是技术问题。"

sentences.text: Surely it should be obvious to the dimmest executive that trust, that most valuable of economic assets, is easily destroyed and hugely expensive to restore – and that few things are more likely to destroy trust than a company letting sensitive personal data get into the wrong hands.
